name: TX-06
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+11 partisan lean favors Ellzey
Incumbency advantage with no polls or expert ratings to shift the picture
model.rationale: The R+11 district, Ellzey's incumbency, and a lopsided fundraising gap leave Minton with no visible path; markets price the race at 95% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings, the forecast stays close to fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending targeting the district would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Jake Ellzey seeks another term in a North Texas district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised roughly $4.7 million and holding $2.5 million on hand, while Democrat Danny Minton has raised about $44,000. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Ellzey about a 95 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals point firmly toward Ellzey: the district's partisan lean, his incumbency advantage, and his fundraising dominance all align. Minton would need an unusual shift in the political environment to make this competitive, and nothing in the available evidence suggests one is underway.
